help.intro: Carts are filled by shoppers on the storefront - nothing here creates or edits one. This screen is for looking: what people are carrying right now, and what it would cost them.
help.step_1_title: The prices here are not stored
help.step_1_body: A cart line records what was picked - the variant, the quantity, the options chosen - and no money at all. Everything under Pricing is worked out against the catalog at the moment you open this window, so a cart from three weeks ago shows what it would cost today, not what it cost then.
help.step_2_body: A cart with no user is an anonymous visitor, identified by a handle their browser holds. That handle is their whole credential, so it is never shown here and you cannot search by it. Signing in folds the guest cart into the account's own, summing the quantities on lines both held, and the guest cart is then deleted.
help.step_3_title: Lines that can no longer be bought
help.step_3_body: A line whose product was withdrawn, fell outside its availability window, or has no price in the cart's currency comes back marked rather than silently dropped - the shopper has to see what happened. Any such line blocks checkout until it is removed.
help.step_4_body: A cart has no status: it exists while somebody is filling it and is deleted the moment it stops being that. Checking out writes the order and removes the cart in the same step, and a cleanup job deletes any cart left untouched past its expiry date. Either way a shopper coming back gets a new cart, never the old one - the order is the record of what was bought.
help.step_5_body: Every row here is a live basket, so there is no status to filter by and nothing removed to bring back. Narrow by user to answer a support question, or by currency to see one market. To trace a sale, start from the order instead - the cart it came from no longer exists.
help.note: Deleting a cart here is a support action, not a cleanup tool - the cleanup job already removes expired carts on its own. It is permanent, and it takes away what a shopper had picked out while they may still be looking at it.
